title:
The "collection" encapsulates data access methods needed by a user interface to interact with the underlying data
of a set of a logical objects in some data repository. The individual objects are instances of models for a single
source type.

A collection maintains state locally about changes made which have not yet been saved to the server. The #add method
changes data locally (applying simple validations), but does not send anything to the server and just marks the
local collection as dirty. Similarly, changes to the models within the collection are buffered. When #save is called,
all pending changes are bundled up and submitted to the server in a single request and if the server responds with a
success status, the collection becomes clean.

Collections support these {@link UiEventSource events}:
 - `change`: any change to the individual models or the loaded set
 - `add`: addition of a model (via #add or #insert)
 - `remove`: removal of a model (via #remove)
 - `save`: the collection was successfully saved to the server
 - `reload`: the collection was reloaded from the server

The collection only manages the data of a set of objects. The presentation is configured using a {@link UiView view}.

It also doesn't act as a controller, that is done by defining a {@link ReactComponent component}. For example,
{@link CollectionGrid} is a generic controller component for collections that presents the contents as a table.

Methods which delegate processing to the server are asynchronous and return a Promise.

@see UiModel
@see UiView
